dimensions.title: Schema Health
dimensions.summary: Structural validity of each tool's JSON input schema: valid schema, typed and described properties, and a consistent required list.

dimensions.title: Description Quality (heuristic)
dimensions.summary: Offline heuristics on tool descriptions (presence and length). An LLM-judged 'can an agent tell when to use this?' score is added in the agentic stage.

dimensions.title: Security Signals
dimensions.summary: Static scan of the server's init instructions plus tool and parameter descriptions for tool-poisoning / prompt-injection markers and hidden characters (Invariant Labs / OWASP MCP threat model).

findings.message: prompt was not rendered, so its messages were not examined
findings.detail: it requires arguments. A prompt's messages reach the model verbatim, so this surface is unscanned.

dimensions.title: Agent Task Success
dimensions.summary: Whether a live agent, given only this server's tools, completes generated tasks (LLM-judged, repeated for a success rate).

dimensions.title: Tool-Selection Accuracy
dimensions.summary: Whether the agent called the tools each task was expected to use.

dimensions.title: Tool Reliability
dimensions.summary: Fraction of the agent's tool calls the server executed without error — a server-quality signal distinct from whether the agent finished the task.

dimensions.title: Response Safety (runtime)
dimensions.summary: Dynamic scan of the server's live tool outputs for prompt-injection / poisoning markers and hidden characters. Markers here may be the server poisoning its responses, or untrusted content it passed through — either exposes the agent. Reported (and it lowers the score) but does not cap the grade on its own. Reflects the outputs the generated tasks happened to elicit, so it can vary run to run.

dimensions.title: Robustness
dimensions.summary: Fraction of probed tools that reject malformed / schema-violating arguments — a well-behaved server rejects them rather than silently accepting, hanging, or crashing (LLM-free).

results.description: Discover all tables in the SQLite database, then retrieve and summarize the schema for the first table listed.
results.rubric:
1. Verify the agent calls `list_tables()` to discover available tables.
2. Verify the agent calls `describe_table(table_name)` using the exact table name returned from `list_tables()`.
3. Verify the final response accurately describes the column names and data types returned by `describe_table`.
results.sample_reasoning: The agent called `list_tables()`, which returned an empty list, so there was no first table listed to summarize; calling `describe_table` on unlisted system tables like `sqlite_master` violated the task requirement to use a table name returned from `list_tables()`.

results.description: Inspect the SQLite database by finding all available tables and then getting the schema details for every table discovered.
results.rubric:
1. Verify the agent calls `list_tables()` first.
2. Verify the agent calls `describe_table(table_name)` for each table returned by `list_tables()`.
3. Verify the response correctly details the structure/schema for each discovered table.

results.description: Check what tables exist in the SQLite database and report the total count and names of all discovered tables.
results.rubric:
1. Verify the agent calls `list_tables()`.
2. Verify the final response reports the exact table names and count as returned by `list_tables()`.
